Package com.csse3200.game.cards

Record Class Card

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.csse3200.game.cards.Card
Record Components:
id - unique identifier, e.g. "strike". Used for lookups, not shown to the player.
name - display name, e.g. "Strike". Shown as the label in UI feedback ("Strike played").
description - flavour/rules text, not currently rendered anywhere but kept for later UI.
trigger - the event name fired on the drop target when this card is played, e.g. "damage".
args - arguments passed to that event, in order, e.g. {10} for "10 damage". 0-3 supported.
skinFile - path to the button style JSON, e.g. "sprites/cards/cardExample.json".
skinAtlas - path to the matching texture atlas.
styleName - the ImageButtonStyle name within skinFile, e.g. "cardStyle".
width - on-screen width in pixels.
height - on-screen height in pixels.
public record Card(String id, String name, String description, String trigger, Object[] args, String skinFile, String skinAtlas, String styleName, float width, float height) extends Record
Immutable definition of a single card: what it's called, what event it fires when played (and with what arguments), and how it should look as a draggable button.

A Card doesn't know how to render or drag itself — toClickableRecord(float, float, Skin) builds a ClickableRecord (variant "drag") that the existing Clickable/DragNDrop machinery already knows how to handle. This keeps card *data* (loaded from configs/cards.json via CardService) separate from the generic UI plumbing.

The Skin itself isn't resolved here — CardService caches Skin instances per skinFile/ skinAtlas pair (the same way ClickableFactory does) and passes the resolved Skin in, so repeated calls don't reload the same texture atlas from disk.
